artworks.title: Sommerso bowl in blue and amber
artworks.summary: A heavy rectangular bowl in sommerso glass from the MURANIQ collection, with a blue layer cased in amber and clear glass.
description: Seen from above, a band of blue glass runs around the well of this thick, rectangular bowl, cased within amber and clear glass. The layers follow the curve of the form, as is typical of sommerso.
Maker, glasshouse and date have not yet been documented, so no attribution is given.

artworks.title: Monumental aquamarine scavo corroso vase
artworks.summary: A large, heavy vase in aquamarine glass with a matt scavo surface, two applied ring handles and an undulating relief around the body. It carries a Seguso Arte Vetro factory label.
description: The rounded body rises into a tall cylindrical neck. Two ring handles of colourless glass are applied on either side of the neck, and a broad undulating relief runs all the way around the lower body. The vase is 32 cm high and 30 cm wide and weighs 7.5 kg, which is heavy for its size.

The surface is matt and finely granular throughout: a scavo finish, which imitates the weathered skin of glass recovered from the ground. The aquamarine colour varies from light turquoise to grey-green and a deeper green, with paler and darker patches. The foot is ground flat and is smoother than the rest of the surface. No engraved signature has been found.

A printed factory label on the lower body reads MURANO ITALY, SEGUSO, arte vetro, around a large stylised S. It is the main evidence for the maker, Seguso Arte Vetro, also known as Seguso AV. That firm should not be confused with Seguso Vetri d'Arte, a different Murano glassworks with its own history and archive.

Auction and reference sources connect Seguso Arte Vetro with the Murano glass artist Livio Seguso (born on Murano in 1930). Dealers have offered closely related vases in aquamarine and in white; the seller of the white example describes it as designed by Livio Seguso and made by Bisazza Vetro in 1993 (see Comparable examples). That makes a link with his designs plausible, but it does not show that he designed this vase. The model, designer and date of this example are still being researched.

marks.location: lower body, just above the foot
marks.observation: Printed factory label with white lettering on a transparent ground, so the glass shows through. MURANO and ITALY run upwards along the left edge; a large stylised S is followed by E / GU / SO, with 'arte vetro' below.
marks.transcriptionNote: Read from the photograph. The S of SEGUSO is the large initial; the remaining letters are stacked as E / GU / SO.
marks.interpretation: Factory label of Seguso Arte Vetro (Seguso AV), Murano. The period in which this label was used has not been established.

assertions.publicNote: Based on the printed Seguso Arte Vetro factory label on the lower body (see Marks & Labels). A label is strong evidence of the firm that made or sold a piece, but labels can be moved or added later, so it supports the attribution without proving it. No catalogue entry or model number has been found yet.
Based on the label, which reads MURANO ITALY.

evidence.locator: white example, dated 1993 by the seller

assertions.publicNote: A working date range, not a documented date. It rests on comparable pieces: a closely related white vase dated 1993 by its seller, and a Livio Seguso work by Seguso Arte Vetro catalogued as c. 1980. It will stay provisional until a catalogue or other document is found.

assertions.statement: Scavo surface, of the kind sold as scavo corroso
assertions.publicNote: The matt, granular and unevenly coloured skin shows the characteristics of scavo, the Murano finish that imitates excavated glass. 'Corroso' refers to a corroded or etched surface. How the surface of this particular piece was produced has not been established.

assertions.statement: Design associated with Livio Seguso: not confirmed

evidence.locator: Livio Seguso work by Seguso Arte Vetro
white example, attributed by the seller

assertions.publicNote: Seguso Arte Vetro is linked with Livio Seguso in auction records, and a dealer attributes a white vase of almost the same form and size to him. No document yet links this model to him, so his name is given as an association, not as the designer of this vase.

artworks.condition: Light surface marks are visible on the matt skin, including small dark specks and fine scratches. A full condition report has not yet been made.

comparables.title: Large Italian Scavo Corroso Aquamarine Glass Urn Vase
stated: Blown glass with a scavo corroso surface, in a 'Classical Roman' style.
comparables.comparison: Very close in colour and form: the same aquamarine tone, tall cylindrical neck, rounded body, two ring handles and undulating relief. The MURANIQ vase is larger (32 × 30 cm) and carries a Seguso Arte Vetro label. The two are probably the same basic design or closely related versions, but no catalogue or model number confirms it.

comparables.title: Seguso for Bisazza White Scavo Corroso Murano Glass Vase 1993 Signed
stated: Designed by Livio Seguso and made by Bisazza Vetro in 1993.
White to cream scavo corroso glass with two round handles.
Part of a Livio Seguso production collection made under Bisazza; the form is related to late-1980s taste influenced by Native American and Navajo pottery.
comparables.comparison: Almost the same height and diameter, with the same rounded body, cylindrical neck, applied ring handles, scavo finish and undulating relief, in white instead of aquamarine. It is the strongest indication of a link with Livio Seguso's designs. It is not known whether the two share a model number, or whether the Seguso Arte Vetro version was made before, during or after the Bisazza version.

established: Murano glass with a printed Seguso Arte Vetro factory label.
Two applied ring handles and a continuous undulating relief around the lower body.
Height 32 cm, width 30 cm, weight 7.5 kg; the foot is ground flat.
Very close in form to an aquamarine vase and a white vase offered by dealers (see Comparable examples).
plausible: A design from the circle of Livio Seguso.
Made in the late 1980s or early 1990s.
The same basic design as the white vase sold as Bisazza, 1993.
A larger version of the aquamarine vase offered by a dealer.
open: Year of production and how many were made.
When this type of Seguso Arte Vetro label was in use.
Whether the aquamarine and white versions belong to the same series, and how Seguso Arte Vetro and Bisazza relate for this model.
